safety_verdicts.content: There is no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated assessment does not explicitly state no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not explicitly documenting "no evidence of cellulitis" slightly reduces clarity of the assessment, but the encounter already frames this as a localized reaction with advice to monitor for spreading redness/warmth that would prompt reassessment for infection. This omission is unlikely to change immediate management or create patient harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Right arm sting site: erythema, blotchy rash, puncture mark visible; no significant swelling
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold physical finding stating no rash seen on the arm; generated asserts visible erythema/blotchy rash and puncture mark on exam.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly documenting erythema/blotchy rash and a visible puncture mark when the gold standard notes no rash could bias subsequent clinicians toward diagnosing a more prominent local reaction or early infection. While unlikely to cause severe outcomes, it could prompt unnecessary monitoring, follow-up, or even antibiotic consideration if taken at face value.
